# Check hook targets in the built image, not in each patch's own bytes

When two patches write the same site, a per-patch check reads the wrong bytes and can miss the jump that ships.

**Category:** hazard · <span class="pill pill-planned">Single source</span>
{ .facts }

**Build:** [E-PM2 firmware 1.6, build 1600](../firmware/epm2-1600.md) · **Cameras:** [Olympus PEN E-PM2](../cameras/epm2.md)

EPM2Mod's hook check decoded each patch on its own, so a later patch's jump from early-loaded code into segment 2 was reported as the earlier patch's jump. The check now decodes the built bytes of every change in early-loaded space, with overlapping changes as one run, and lists stock pointers that a change rewrites.

> **What happens:** A jump into late-loaded code passed the check and shipped from rc.3 to v2026.11.20 on the E-PM2.

**Symptoms:** [Starts slowly](index.md#slow-start); [Fails to start, restarts or loops at power-on](index.md#start-failure)

## Observations

- **Static analysis** ([EPM2Mod](../projects/epm2mod.md)): The rebuilt check finds that jump as the one failure of the pinned spot-af-2 build. Its audit lists 187 transfers out of patched early-loaded code, 88 of them into segments 2 or 3. Source: [EPM2Mod slow cold start investigation](../sources/epm2.slow-boot.md).
